lectures.title: Rockets in news: private, ISRO and defence rockets

items: India's first successful private orbital launch
**18 November 2022:** Skyroot's **Vikram-S** became India's first privately developed rocket to reach space. Mission: **Prarambh**. It attained an altitude of approximately 89.5 km.
**18 July 2026:** **Vikram-1** completed India's first successful private orbital launch under **Mission Aagaman**.
**May 2026:** Skyroot became India's first space-tech unicorn, valued at US$1.1 billion.
**Pawan Kumar Chandana:** Skyroot Aerospace's co-founder and CEO. He is an IIT Kharagpur alumnus and former ISRO scientist.
First privately developed Indian rocket to reach space

parts.t: EVEREST: privately developed FFSC rocket engine
items: **Engine name:** EVEREST, India's privately developed FFSC rocket engine.
**EVEREST** is India's first fully integrated, privately developed **Full-Flow Staged Combustion (FFSC)** rocket engine.
**Testing status:** As of 22 August 2026, full-scale integrated hot-fire testing was still pending.
**Performance figures:** Reported performance figures were company-stated design targets, not demonstrated operational performance.
**Pre-burners:** Fuel and oxidiser pass through separate pre-burners.
**Turbines:** The gases produced drive turbines connected to pumps.
**Main chamber:** The propellants subsequently enter the main combustion chamber.
**Result:** This arrangement allows both propellants to contribute to the main combustion process.
**First LOX-methane high-thrust engine:** EVEREST is described as India's first LOX-methane high-thrust engine.
**Fourth commercial FFSC development globally**, after: 1. SpaceX, 2. Stoke Space, 3. LandSpace.
**Reusable launches:** Potentially supports reusable launches carrying up to 30 tonnes to Low Earth Orbit, according to the company's stated targets.
**Manufacturing:** The development uses advanced manufacturing, including India's largest industrial 3D printer.
India's first indigenous **350 kg-thrust-class expendable turbojet engine**.
**Industry partner:** Azad Engineering. **Location of industry partner:** Hyderabad.
**Successfully realised and delivered to GTRE:** 22 July 2026.
**Indigenous:** Indigenous design and manufacturing of a complex propulsion system.
**Cooperation:** Cooperation between DRDO laboratories and private manufacturers.
**Progress:** Progress in precision engineering, advanced metallurgy and thermal management.
**Imports:** Potential to reduce dependence on imported compact propulsion systems after successful testing and production approval.

parts.t: ISRO: LVM3-M6 mission and CE20 engine
items: **Satellite launched:** BlueBird Block-2. **Satellite owner:** AST SpaceMobile, USA.
**Largest:** Described as the largest commercial communication satellite ever deployed into LEO.
**Antenna:** Its 223 m² phased-array antenna supports direct-to-device communication.
**Constellation:** The constellation aims to provide 4G and 5G voice calls, video calls, messaging, streaming and data services.
**BlueBird Block-2** was the heaviest payload launched into LEO in LVM3's history.
**Engine:** CE20 cryogenic engine. **Associated launch vehicle:** LVM3.
**Test centre:** ISRO Propulsion Complex, Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu.
**Mission link:** The test was associated with LVM3's seventh operational mission.
**Satellite:** EOS-05 Earth Observation Satellite. **Launch vehicle:** GSLV-F17.
**Launch site:** Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.
**Orbit:** Geosynchronous orbit. **Orbit-raising engine:** Liquid Apogee Motor (LAM).
**EOS-05** is India's first satellite to carry out imaging from a geosynchronous orbit.
**Achievement:** First artificial satellite launched into space.
**4 October:** The date 4 October is associated with the beginning of World Space Week.
**Record:** Two orbital launches took place only 38 minutes apart: the shortest interval between two orbital launches conducted by a single launch provider.
**First launch:** 9:12 p.m. EDT, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida.
**Second launch:** 9:50 p.m. EDT, Vandenberg Space Force Base, California.
**Previous record:** 65 minutes, set on 31 August 2024 through two consecutive Starlink launches.
**System:** Pinaka Long Range Guided Rocket (LRGR). **Developer:** DRDO.
**Test date:** 8 July 2026. **Test location:** Integrated Test Range (ITR), Chandipur, Odisha.
**Test date:** 3 February 2026. **Location:** Integrated Test Range, Chandipur, Odisha.
**Purpose:** Demonstration of advanced air-to-air missile propulsion technology; a successful technology demonstration.
**What is SFDR?** It is a propulsion technology based on a ducted ramjet. It is intended to support advanced air-to-air missiles.
**Mahe-class:** The Indian Navy's Mahe-class Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC) is equipped with an indigenous anti-submarine rocket launcher.
**The vessel also carries:** Abhay hull-mounted sonar; lightweight torpedoes; Maareech Advanced Torpedo Decoy System.
**Roles:** Underwater surveillance, coastal anti-submarine warfare and low-intensity maritime operations.
**INS Mangrol:** one of the vessels equipped with these systems.
**Test location:** Pokhran Field Firing Range, Rajasthan.
Launch site for Vikram-1 and GSLV-F17, among other missions
Pinaka LRGR, SFDR and defence propulsion research
Manufacturing partner for GTRE's turbojet engine

parts.t: National Policy on Biofuels and ethanol blending
items: **2022 amendment:** advanced the target to E20 by Ethanol Supply Year (ESY) 2025–26.
EBP Programme launched in 9 States and 4 UTs
National Policy on Biofuels targeted E20 by 2030
Policy amended; E20 target advanced to ESY 2025–26
Minimum RON 95 requirement for notified blended petrol
**Energy:** Energy security and reduced crude-oil dependence.
**Farmers:** Support to farmers and rural industries.
**Approved by:** the Union Cabinet and Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
**Earlier policy:** Updates and extends the New Investment Policy, 2012.
**Objectives:** Promote domestic urea production; achieve urea self-reliance; encourage investment in gas-based urea manufacturing plants.
**New plants:** Establishment of 8–9 new gas-based plants.
**Capacity:** Additional annual production capacity of approximately 10 million tonnes.
**Costs:** Separates fixed and variable production costs.
**Foreign-exchange risk:** Fixed costs converted into Indian rupees after four years at the prevailing exchange rate to reduce foreign-exchange risk.

items: **UDAN:** Regional Connectivity Scheme – UDAN launched on 21 October 2016.
**RCS-UDAN** stands for Regional Connectivity Scheme – Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik.
**Policy:** The scheme follows the National Civil Aviation Policy, 2016.
**Objective:** Affordable and economically viable air connectivity to unserved and underserved regions.
**Developed by:** NITI Aayog in collaboration with WRI India.
**Measures:** progress of electric mobility across States and Union Territories.
